entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-2cv4-cqwr-gwf7: uv: Path traversal on Windows through wheel extraction
entry.content:
uv: Path traversal on Windows through wheel extraction

Aliases: CVE-2026-104843, PYSEC-2026-4305

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:N/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • uv — fixed in 0.12.18
  • uv — fixed in 0.12.18

### Impact In versions of uv from 0.12.7 to 0.12.18 on Windows, uv could be induced into writing a file outside of the installation prefix during wheel installation. A malicious wheel could use this to place an executable outside of the intended environment, including in a directory already present on the user's PATH. This vulnerability only affects Windows hosts; no other platforms are affected. ### Patches uv 0.12.18 and newer address this vulnerability. Users are encouraged to upgrade to 0.12.18. ### Workarounds There is no workaround other than upgrading to uv 0.12.18.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-m4ch-rfv5-x5g3: git2-rs fails to verify SSH keys by default
entry.content:
git2-rs fails to verify SSH keys by default

Aliases: CVE-2023-22742, GHSA-8643-3wh5-rmjq, RUSTSEC-2023-0003

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • libgit2-sys — fixed in 0.14.2
  • libgit2-sys — fixed in 0.13.5
  • git2 — fixed in 0.16.1

The git2 and libgit2-sys crates are Rust wrappers around the [libgit2](https://libgit2.org/) C library. It was discovered that libgit2 1.5.0 and below did not verify SSH host keys when establishing an SSH connection, exposing users of the library to Man-In-the-Middle attacks. The libgit2 team assigned [CVE-2023-22742](https://github.com/libgit2/libgit2/security/advisories/GHSA-8643-3wh5-rmjq) to this vulnerability. The following versions of the libgit2-sys Rust crate have been released: * libgit2-sys 0.14.2, updating the underlying libgit2 C library to version 1.5.1. * libgit2-sys 0.13.5, updating the underlying libgit2 C library to version 1.4.5. A new git2 crate version has also been released, 0.16.1. This version only bumps its libgit2-sys dependency to ensure no vulnerable libgit2-s…

entry.title: [NEW] RUSTSEC-2026-0348: Brotli certificate decompression can allocate up to 1 GiB before authentication
entry.content:
Brotli certificate decompression can allocate up to 1 GiB before authentication

Aliases: GHSA-h2v8-394m-p7vv

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L

Affected:

  • rustls — fixed in 0.23.46

The built-in Brotli certificate decompressor (enabled by the non-default `brotli` crate feature) bounded the size of the decompressed output, but accepted a peer-selected history window. Brotli's large-window extension was enabled, so a five-byte header could cause an allocation of 1 GiB. A peer can abort a process whose allocator cannot satisfy that request. No trusted certificate is required by the attacker. Affected configurations are: - clients that enable the `brotli` feature and connect to a malicious server, and - servers that enable the `brotli` feature and request client certificates. Applications that do not enable the `brotli` feature are not affected.

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/rustls
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0348.html
  • https://github.com/rustls/rustls/pull/3297

entry.title: [NEW] RUSTSEC-2026-0346: `Debug` impls for client session values expose TLS secrets
entry.content:
`Debug` impls for client session values expose TLS secrets

Aliases: GHSA-c8m5-c952-6cm4

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:H/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • rustls — fixed in 0.23.46

The `Debug` implementations of `Tls12ClientSessionValue` and `Tls13ClientSessionValue` were derived, and so included the TLS 1.2 master secret or TLS 1.3 resumption PSK in their output. Custom `ClientSessionStore` implementations that format these values with `Debug` (for example, when logging) could disclose these secrets to readers of the logs. This conflicts with rustls's [key-material redaction policy](https://github.com/rustls/rustls/blob/99f2358cae2954837dbb866faf6727de75489ab9/SECURITY.md#boundary-public-api). Ordinary connection and built-in session cache `Debug` output is redacted and is not affected.

  • https://crates.io/crates/rustls
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0346.html

entry.title: [NEW] RUSTSEC-2026-0349: Unauthenticated ServerHello can downgrade later connections to classical key exchange
entry.content:
Unauthenticated ServerHello can downgrade later connections to classical key exchange

Aliases: GHSA-w44r-93j7-qv28

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • rustls — fixed in 0.23.46

The client recorded the server-selected key exchange group for each server name when processing the ServerHello, before the server was authenticated. This record is used to predict which key share to send in future ClientHellos to that server name. A network attacker can answer one connection attempt with a ServerHello selecting X25519, and then close the connection. Later ClientHellos for that name carry only an X25519 key share, while `supported_groups` still lists X25519MLKEM768 first. If the genuine server accepts that share rather than sending a HelloRetryRequest for its preferred hybrid group, the handshake completes with classical-only key exchange and no error. This persists for as long as the entry stays in the client's session store. The impact is loss of post-quantum confident…

  • https://crates.io/crates/rustls
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0349.html

entry.title: [NEW] RUSTSEC-2026-0347: Buffered application data sent to outer server after ECH rejection
entry.content:
Buffered application data sent to outer server after ECH rejection

Aliases: GHSA-vp88-798v-h67f

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • rustls — fixed in 0.23.46

When a server rejects Encrypted Client Hello (ECH), the client completes the handshake using the outer ClientHello and authenticates the server against the ECH config's `public_name`. At the end of that handshake, rustls encrypted and queued any application data buffered via `ClientConnection::writer()` *before* queueing the `ech_required` alert. The application correctly receives `Error::PeerIncompatible(ServerRejectedEncryptedClientHello)`, but the next `write_tls()` call (needed to send the alert) also sends the buffered application data. Plaintext meant for the inner server therefore goes to the client-facing server named by `public_name`.
